title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 57-58
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 57 to 58 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'महर्षिः कपिलाचार्यः कृतज्ञो मेदिनीपतिः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 57 to 58 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 57 to 58.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 57 to 58** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **महर्षिः कपिलाचार्यः कृतज्ञो मेदिनीपतिः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**महर्षिः कपिलाचार्यः कृतज्ञो मेदिनीपतिः । त्रिपदस्त्रिदशाध्यक्षो महाशृङ्गः कृतान्तकृत् ॥** **महावराहो गोविन्दः सुषेणः कनकाङ्गदी । गुह्यो गभीरो गहनो गुप्तश्चक्रगदाधरः ॥**

He is the great sage Kapila. The one who remembers every kindness, the lord of the earth, is that God of gods. He took three strides, presides over the gods, bears the great horn, and brings an end even to death. He is the Great Boar and Govinda. The one with the noble army, wearing golden armlets, is that God of gods. Secret, profound, unfathomable and hidden, bearing the discus and the mace.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 57 to 58 mean?
faq.a: He is the great sage Kapila. The one who remembers every kindness, the lord of the earth, is that God of gods. He took three strides, presides over the gods, bears the great horn, and brings an end even to death. He is the Great Boar and Govinda. The one with the noble army, wearing golden armlets, is that God of gods. Secret, profound, unfathomable and hidden, bearing the discus and the mace.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
